notes: All seven contract tests pass, plus the full truck-geometry suite and the packet Done-when commands (fmt/clippy -D warnings/test). Implementation notes: (1) Only the NORMAL is carried through the double reflection; the binormal is always re-derived as t x n after each re-orthonormalization (contract clause 4 fixes t x n == b and re-orthonormalizes only the normal). The canonical method also reflects the binormal, but that value is dead — it is always overwritten by tangent.cross(normal) before emission — so the observable frame is bit-identical to the full canonical transcription; clippy -D warnings (unused-assignments) independently forced dropping it. (2) 'the queried s as the final station' is read as the transport sequence ending AT s: grid stations up to and including the station at/before s, with s appended as the last element when s is not exactly on a grid station. This is the only reading consistent with on-grid queries returning the frame at the queried s (tests 1,3,5,7 query on-grid s and assert on those frames); appending s after s_max would return frame(s_max) for on-grid s. The sequence is deterministic from (spine, initial_normal, s) alone, so evaluation-order independence holds bit-exactly. (3) The dispatcher's ZeroTangent refusal at the queried s is not duplicated; the transport derives its own start tangent at s_min and, per contract clause 3/5, refuses ZeroTangent at the parameter where a derived tangent vanishes. (4) &dyn Spine was object-safe; no generic spelling needed. Noted for the orchestrator: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports pre-existing drift in examples/step_face_timing.rs and tests/geometry_fingerprint.rs (files outside write_allow, untouched here); tests/geometry_fingerprint bracket_tessellates_to_a_known_mesh fails identically on the base commit (golden drift, left 1875 / right 1814) and tests/bspcurve parameter_random_tests is a seed-dependent proptest (passes 5/5 in isolation, passed in the final full run).
